recent_posts.title: Genkit Dart vs Firebase AI Logic in 2026 - Which Should Flutter Developers Use?
recent_posts.summary: A comparison of two Google AI integration approaches for Flutter developers: Firebase AI Logic (client-side SDK for quick, secure Gemini access) and Genkit Dart (full-stack AI framework for complex agentic workflows). Covers use cases, pros/cons, pricing, performance, and a decision framework. Firebase AI Logic wins for simple, fast client-side features; Genkit Dart is recommended for production apps needing tool calling, persistent memory, backend logic, or cost optimization. The author recommends learning both, starting with Firebase AI Logic for speed and graduating to Genkit Dart for scale.

recent_posts.title: Get Started with Firebase AI Logic + Flutter: Build A Simple Caption Generator
recent_posts.summary: Firebase AI Logic (formerly Vertex AI in Firebase) provides Flutter apps with direct access to Google's Gemini models. A step-by-step walkthrough shows how to set up the firebase_ai package, initialize Firebase in a Flutter project, and build a simple caption generator using the Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite model. The guide also covers production best practices including App Check, Firebase Auth, Remote Config for prompts, Firestore caching, and when to offload complex workflows to Genkit on the backend.

recent_posts.title: Genkit Dart for Flutter Developers: Build Full-Stack AI Apps in 2026 (Getting Started)
recent_posts.summary: Genkit Dart is Google's open-source framework that lets Flutter developers build full-stack AI apps entirely in Dart. This getting-started guide walks through setting up a Genkit Dart backend, defining typed AI flows using schemas, integrating the Gemini API, and connecting the backend to a Flutter frontend via an HTTP endpoint using shelf. The tutorial covers installing the Genkit CLI and packages, building a content generator flow with structured input/output schemas, testing with the Genkit Developer UI, and exposing the flow as a REST API consumed by the Flutter client.

recent_posts.title: Gemini CLI + Flutter: The Most Powerful AI Coding Assistant Workflow in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A guide to setting up Gemini CLI for Flutter development, covering installation, VS Code integration, and prompt templates for code generation, refactoring, and debugging. Includes demo commands for generating Riverpod providers, fixing Impeller rendering jank, scaffolding production screens, and running targeted tests from the terminal. Also covers common pitfalls and workflow tips.

recent_posts.title: Stitch + Antigravity + Flutter: Build Apps with AI Agents in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of an AI-assisted Flutter app development workflow using Google's Stitch (AI design agent) and Antigravity (agentic IDE). Stitch generates UI designs from text prompts, which are then exported via MCP connectors to Antigravity, where an AI agent writes the full Flutter/Dart codebase following Clean Architecture with Riverpod. The demo builds a Daily Habit Tracker app from prompt to running emulator in about 10-12 minutes. Includes setup steps, example prompts, best practices, and limitations of the agentic approach.

How to Push Over-the-Air (OTA) Flutter Updates with Shorebird - Complete 2026 Guide
recent_posts.summary: Shorebird's Code Push lets Flutter developers push over-the-air updates to Dart code without waiting for App Store or Play Store review cycles. The guide covers installing the Shorebird CLI, initializing a project, creating a first release, and pushing a patch live. Key points include that only Dart code can be patched (native plugins still require store updates), patches are typically under 1MB, rollback is automatic, and the service is free for small usage. Best practices include testing on real devices, using shorebird doctor, handling patch failures gracefully, and integrating with CI/CD pipelines.

recent_posts.title: How to Build Responsive Flutter Apps for Phones, Foldables, Tablets & Web (2026)
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to building responsive Flutter UIs that work across phones, foldables, tablets, and web in 2026. Covers using MediaQuery for screen dimensions and orientation, LayoutBuilder with breakpoints (mobile/tablet/desktop), and flutter_screenutil for pixel-perfect scaling. Includes best practices like SafeArea usage, max-width constraints for large screens, and performance targets under 8ms per frame.

recent_posts.title: Flutter Beginner Tutorial 2026: Build Your First App (Setup + Modern Best Practices)
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly Flutter tutorial covering installation, project setup, and building a counter app using Riverpod for state management. Walks through creating a new Flutter project, adding dependencies, setting up ProviderScope, creating a counter provider, and building a home page with increment/decrement functionality. Includes complete code examples for main.dart, provider setup, and UI implementation with hot reload support.

recent_posts.title: Learn Dart Programming Language: A Beginner's Guide
recent_posts.summary: Dart fundamentals are covered through practical examples: variables (var, final, const), operators (arithmetic, logical, relational), string interpolation, conditionals (if/else, ternary, switch), collections (Lists and Maps), for loops, functions with optional parameters, and null safety features. Each concept includes code snippets demonstrating syntax and common use cases for mobile app development, with emphasis on type safety and null-aware operators introduced in Dart 2.12.

top_posts.title: Vibe Coding: Build A Complete App From Scratch In Minutes Using GitHub Copilot.
top_posts.summary: A senior engineer shares their journey from skepticism to adoption of GitHub Copilot after testing it on tutorial projects. They demonstrate building a Flutter app called "Mood Mixer" that captures selfies, detects emotions, and generates Spotify playlists using only AI prompts and no manual coding. The piece explores how AI tools can serve as effective assistants for scaffolding, state management, and function improvements rather than complete replacements for developer skills.
